title: Evaluation of Various State of the Art Head Pose Estimation Algorithms for Clinical Scenarios
metricDefinition: Video-based yaw, pitch, and roll estimates are compared with an optoelectronic reference; reported differences characterize estimator accuracy only.

extractionLocations.description: Head-pose methods, inputs, and performance characteristics.
Bias by yaw, pitch, and roll plane; retained only as measurement limitation.

study.deviceAndEnvironment: Laboratory RGB camera and optoelectronic reference

measurements.definition: Difference between video-estimated and reference yaw, pitch, and roll.
measurements.calculationMethod: Algorithm outputs compared with optoelectronic motion capture.
notes: Values are algorithm accuracy, not permissible behavior.

reportedFindings.summary: Estimator error varies by algorithm and movement plane, supporting deployment-specific validation and quality gating.

faceFitMappings.reason: Estimator bias is not an observed baseline-relative yaw displacement.
Estimator bias is not an observed baseline-relative pitch displacement.
Estimator bias is not an observed baseline-relative roll displacement.
Accuracy limitations motivate a quality gate but do not define Face-Fit frame availability.

thresholdAssessment.reason: Reported angle differences measure algorithm validity and cannot become interview-behavior boundaries.

limitations: The clinical laboratory context and single-participant validation do not transfer directly to webcam interviews.
Head orientation and gaze remain distinct constructs.
